D.t: Jamie Ager leads by 8.0 in the forecast and wins 92% of simulations. The cushion is about 25,147 votes; a one point swing is about 1,580 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +0.6 and D +15.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
Registered Democrats cast 41% of the 1,544,874 ballots in North Carolina so far, against 24% for the other party. That is 0.9 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

R.t: Jennifer Balkcom trails by 8.0 and wins 8% of simulations. Closing it takes about 12,574 voters switching sides, or 25,147 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +15.3 and D +0.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
Registered Republicans cast 24% of the 1,544,874 ballots in North Carolina so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 0.9 points better for Republicans than the forecast expected by now.
